ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag required — the driver's arrival tap was within the 200 m data-layer radius, so NS-2's flag trigger is not met.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat (F9–F11), the complaint and the driver statement (F13) contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; dispute type is no-show, not safety. safety_concern = none.

Route to rule: the fee is a cancellation fee, `cancelled_by = driver` with the driver asserting the rider no-showed ("Waited more than 3 min, cancelling", F11; F13) → NS-0 sends this to NS-1/NS-2. RydeX is a non-metered service; the fee on record is $6.61 [F4, F7].

NS-1 elements:
(i) Arrival indication — satisfied, but by platform auto-detection at 14:03:20 [F5], not by a driver tap; the driver's own "I'm Here" tap came later, at 14:06:15 [F6]. The record must be read as written: arrival was platform_auto.
(ii) GPS at the pick-up point at the moment of "I'm Here" — satisfied: 178 m from the pickup [F6], within the 200 m data-layer radius (G2), so the NS-2 flag trigger (m_from_pickup_at_tap > 200) is not met.
(iii) Continuous wait at the pickup beyond 3 minutes after the tap — NOT satisfied. The driver tapped at 14:06:15 [F6] and cancelled at 14:09:55 [F4/F11]; the record gives only 3 min 40 s within 200 m after the tap [F6], i.e. ≤ 3 minutes of the post-tap wait that NS-1(iii) requires (needs > 3 min / ≥ 3:01, `within_200m_after_tap_s` > 180). His stationary 4 min 0 s block (14:05:55–14:09:55, 179 m from pickup) [F3] largely predates the tap and cannot be counted; the cumulative 5 min 55 s within 200 m [F2] also includes pre-tap time, and the rule expressly excludes time spent nearby before the tap. The 8 min 55 s from acceptance and the 6 min 35 s from platform arrival [F4, F5] are not the statutory waiting clock either — that clock starts at the "I'm Here" indication. F13's claim of waiting "more than 3 minutes" is a post-hoc statement and is overridden by the gps/timeline records. No record threshold overrides the default (the file carries no `no_show_threshold_min`), and `free_wait_time_min` would not be a threshold in any event.

Because NS-1(iii) fails on at least one element → NS-2: the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider as a voucher (NS-7). Note the rider's own message [F10] shows she was at the entrance and could not see the car parked 179 m away [F3, F9], consistent with a genuine availability problem rather than an uncontactable no-show.

Evidence status: sufficient — GPS and timeline settle arrival, tap position, and post-tap waiting time; the chat is complete and fully timestamped [F12]. Traffic [F14, F15] is irrelevant: this is a no-show dispute, not a route deviation. F17/F18 profiles are not relied on for the outcome (and no RD-6 clause applies, since there is no upheld route finding here — the driver's one upheld dispute is a no-show [F18]).

Amount: $6.61 (full cancellation fee).

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement that he 'pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes' is a claim not backed by the system records: the tap was at 14:06:15 [F6] and only 3 min 40 s within 200 m is recorded after it, i.e. the post-tap continuous wait did not exceed 3 minutes (NS-1(iii)). System records (gps/timeline) override statements.

Platform-recorded arrival at 14:03:20 and the 6 min 35 s to cancellation do not satisfy NS-1(iii): the waiting clock runs from the arrival indication, and the record here shows the driver moved and only held within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the 14:06:15 tap [F6]; the pre-tap stationary/within-radius periods are excluded by the clause.
